translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n592, printed p. 584, heads 14 May `XIV. St. BONIFACE, m.` and rubricates `All as in Mass V. p. 470, except COLLECT. Da, quaesumus.` -- so the day prints its own Collect only, and its Secret is Mass V's. Mass V is `Protexisti`, of a Martyr in Paschal time; leaf n480, printed p. 472, prints under it `SECRET. Of a Martyr not a Bishop.` with no name in it, word for word the 1962's `Muneribus nostris, quaesumus Domine`. Boniface is a martyr and not a bishop, and 14 May falls in Paschal time, so that is the form the pointer reaches. Page-image collation confirms that this historical English body answers the complete target Latin identity; publication is limited to the 1861 wording and does not claim that Cummiskey appoints the 1962 celebration.
